Definition: properly, to be weighty; but used only in the sense of lapidation or its contrary (as if a delapidation)
BiblicalUsage: çâqal is one of those words that sounds small and turns out to matter. It means to be weighty, used of stoning, and it shows up 20 times across the Old Testament. In 1 Kings it carries the full weight of what it says, and the other passages agree.
TheologicalSignificance: To me, çâqal is a reminder that God means what He says. To be weighty, used of stoning is the word He chose for it, and I take it seriously.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
